title: Finite graded extensions induce finite surjective Proj maps
statement: Let $C=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}C_n$ and $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be commutative nonnegatively graded rings and let $\iota:C\hookrightarrow A$ be an injective graded ring homomorphism, meaning $\iota(C_n)\subseteq A_n$ for every $n$. Assume $C$ is a finite type $C_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $A$ is finitely generated as a $C$-module via $\iota$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then the canonical Proj map $r:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Proj}(C)$ [def-pc-proj] is defined on all of $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$, and is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For every homogeneous $f\in C_d$, $d>0$, its inverse image of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\iota(f))$, and on these affine standard opens the map is induced by $C_{(f),0}\to A_{(\iota(f)),0}$, $c/f^m\mapsto\iota(c)/\iota(f)^m$, where the subscripts mean the degree-zero parts of homogeneous localizations. No equality $C_0=A_0$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), applied to a module-finite injective graded map; affine finiteness and homogeneous lying-over are the additional graded-integrality argument used for the invariant Proj construction in Rydh Proposition 4.7. The source lemma defines the map and its chart formula; this finite-extension statement is an agent formulation, to be split separately.

proof.text: Choose finitely many $C$-module generators of $A$ and replace them by all their homogeneous components; they still generate, since their span contains the original generators. Include $1$, and write the resulting homogeneous generators as $a_j\in A_{e_j}$, with $N=\max_j e_j$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. For homogeneous $a\in A_n$ with $n>N$, express $a$ in these generators and project to degree $n$: $a=\sum_j\iota(c_j)a_j$ with $c_j\in C_{n-e_j}\subseteq C_+$. Now let $\mathfrak q$ be a point of $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj]. Choose homogeneous $a\in A_t\setminus\mathfrak q$, $t>0$, and $k$ with $kt>N$. If every positive-degree homogeneous element of $C$ had image in $\mathfrak q$, the displayed expression for $a^k$ would put $a^k$ in $\mathfrak q$, contradicting primality. Thus $\mathfrak q\in D_+(\iota(f))$ for some homogeneous $f\in C_d$, $d>0$. These opens cover all of $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$; no equality of degree-zero rings was used.

source.place: Homogeneous-component argument as in the proof of Tag 00K0 (lemma-graded-module-fg); applied to the domain U(psi) in Constructions Tag 01MY

proof.text: For each homogeneous $f\in C_d$, $d>0$, define $\alpha_f:C_{(f),0}\to A_{(\iota(f)),0}$ by $c/f^m\mapsto\iota(c)/\iota(f)^m$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. It respects degrees because $\iota$ is graded. A relation $f^k(f^n c-f^m b)=0$ is sent to the corresponding relation in $A$, so the formula is well defined and preserves sums, products and one. It is injective: if the image of $c/f^m$ is zero, then $\iota(f)^k\iota(c)=0$ for some $k$, and injectivity of $\iota$ gives $f^kc=0$. Thus $c/f^m=0$. By [def-pc-proj] and [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha_f)$ gives a morphism $r_f:D_+(\iota(f))\to D_+(f)$, which we also regard as a morphism to $\operatorname{Proj}(C)$.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), condition (2) and fraction construction; injectivity is checked directly from the localization relation

proof.text: Check agreement on overlaps, rather than assuming it. If $f\in C_d$ and $g\in C_e$ have positive degrees, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] identifies the intersection of the two source charts with the principal open of $\iota(g)^d/\iota(f)^e$ in the $\iota(f)$ chart, and the intersection of the target charts with the principal open of $g^d/f^e$. The map $\alpha_f$ sends the latter element to the former. Thus $r_f$ on the source intersection factors through $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)=D_+(fg)$; the same holds for $r_g$. Under the restriction maps, which are graded localization maps by [def-pc-proj], both induced homomorphisms from $C_{(fg),0}$ to $A_{(\iota(fg)),0}$ send $c/(fg)^m$ to $\iota(c)/(\iota(f)\iota(g))^m$. This follows by applying $\iota$ to numerator and denominator before or after further localization, using the fraction relation of [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. All elements have these fraction representatives, so the homomorphisms, and hence their spectrum maps [def-weil-affine-spectrum], agree.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), last paragraph of its proof; chart overlaps are Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), (1)(e),(f)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to the open cover of Step 1 and the morphisms $r_f$ of Steps 2--3, with common target $\operatorname{Proj}(C)$. It produces a unique scheme morphism $r:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Proj}(C)$ restricting to those chart maps. The fraction formulas specify the canonical Proj map of Tag 01MY on its natural domain, and Step 1 proves that domain is the entire source.

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), existence by gluing the standard-open morphisms

proof.text: Fix homogeneous $f\in C_d$ of positive degree. On any source chart $D_+(\iota(g))$, with $g\in C_e$ and $e>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection] describes the inverse image of the target open $D_+(f)$ by the nonvanishing of $f^e/g^d$ in the target $g$ chart. Its pullback by the fraction formula is $\iota(f)^e/\iota(g)^d$, whose principal open in the source chart is exactly $D_+(\iota(f))\cap D_+(\iota(g))$, by the same cited intersection formula. Here the inverse image of an affine principal open under a spectrum morphism is the principal open of the image element: a contracted prime contains an element exactly when the original prime contains its image [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since the source charts cover, $r^{-1}(D_+(f))=D_+(\iota(f))$. Step 2 therefore gives the asserted ring map on the whole inverse image of each standard affine open [def-pc-proj].

source.place: Tag 01MY (lemma-morphism-proj), condition (2), using Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) on each source chart

proof.text: View $A=\bigoplus_n A_n$ as the graded $C$-module $M$, with action $c\cdot a=\iota(c)a$. This action is graded and $M$ is finite by hypothesis; $C$ is finite type over $C_0$, so all hypotheses of [lem-per-finite-graded-module-dehomogenization] hold. Its degree-zero module fractions $a/f^m$ identify with $a/\iota(f)^m$ in $A_{(\iota(f)),0}$: both have $a\in A_{md}$, and both impose equality after multiplication by a power of $\iota(f)$. The scalar action is precisely $\alpha_f$. Hence the chart ring map is module-finite. The target standard opens cover by the point description in [def-pc-proj], and Step 5 identifies their inverse images as affine. Condition (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] now proves that $r$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 07Z2 (lemma-dehomogenize-finite-type), (2); global criterion: Morphisms Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local), (2) implies (1)

proof.text: Each $\alpha_f$ is injective by Step 2 and module-finite by Step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] it is integral. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] to this actual chart ring map: every prime of $C_{(f),0}$ is the contraction of a prime of $A_{(\iota(f)),0}$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}(\alpha_f)$ is surjective. The affine chart identifications [def-pc-proj] and spectrum functoriality [def-weil-affine-spectrum] identify this with the restriction of $r$ over $D_+(f)$. Every target point lies in a standard chart, so it has a preimage in that chart inverse image. This is surjectivity of $r$ in [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The proof includes nilpotent $f$ (the charts are empty) and empty Proj; it never assumes $C_0=A_0$.

source.place: Tags 00GK (lemma-finite-is-integral), 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective), applied to the chart maps from Constructions Tag 01MY

proof_origin.place: Agent synthesis of Tag 01MY chart construction with Algebra 07Z2(2), 00GK, 00GQ and Morphisms 01WI; the cover and injectivity arguments are written out.
